question: A 19-year-old man comes to the emergency department for right wrist pain and swelling 2 hours after falling on an outstretched hand while playing softball. The pain worsened when he attempted to pitch after the fall. He has eczema and type 1 diabetes mellitus. Current medications include insulin and topical clobetasol. He appears uncomfortable. Examination shows multiple lichenified lesions over his forearms. The right wrist is swollen and tender; range of motion is limited by pain. There is tenderness to palpation in the area between the tendons of the abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, and extensor pollicis longus muscle. The thumb can be opposed actively towards the other fingers. Muscle strength of the right hand is decreased. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Fall on outstretched hand -> acute wrist pain and swelling -> worsened pain with pitching -> possible musculoskeletal injury -> 70% CHAIN: Eczema and type 1 diabetes mellitus -> insulin and clobetasol use -> skin lesions and lichenification -> 80% CHAIN: Examination findings of tenderness between specific tendons -> possible De Quervain's tenosynovitis -> 60% CHAIN: Decreased muscle strength in the right hand -> nerve or muscle involvement -> possible nerve compression or injury -> 70% CHAIN: Overall clinical presentation with wrist pain, swelling, limited range of motion, and tenderness -> likely musculoskeletal injury -> 80% CHAIN: Based on the examination findings and mechanism of injury -> likely Scaphoid fracture -> 70%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the 19-year-old man with right wrist pain, swelling, and limited range of motion is Scaphoid fracture. The examination findings and mechanism of injury support this diagnosis, despite the presence of eczema and type 1 diabetes mellitus, which are not directly related to the musculoskeletal injury. The evidence paths do not provide additional relevant information for this specific case.
